Brendan — thanks for the clear list. Attached are two artifacts: a redlined TOMs exhibit (redlines_TOMs_v3.docx) and a short SOW for HSMVault (HSM_SOW_v1.pdf). High-level responses below and proposed language to include in the exhibit.

Proposed TOMs language (excerpt):
- Key Management: "Customer data encryption keys used at rest will be protected by Hardware Security Modules (HSM) certified at FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or above. Redwood supports both Redwood-managed HSMs and customer-managed HSM (BYO-HSM) integrations using KMIP. Key wrapping is performed using an envelope-key model; master keys reside in the HSM and are never exported in plaintext."
- Subprocessors: "HSM vendors that process cryptographic operations on behalf of Redwood will be listed as subprocessors. Subprocessor onboarding shall follow Redwood's Subprocessor Onboarding Standard; typical onboarding time is 10-25 business days depending on evidence requested. In exceptional cases, Redwood will provide a written remediation plan to meet customer SLA constraints."
- Audit & Attestation: "Cryptographic key usage and administrative actions are logged to an immutable audit stream with retention of 24 months by default. Upon lawful request, Redwood will provide remote attestation reports or HSM vendor-signed evidence within 10 business days subject to NDA and acceptable use constraints."

Notes: the SOW includes a liability appendix that we can carve into procurement if needed. If Acme requires a strict 30-day hard SLA we can flag it for SOC/ops signoff but will push back on penalties tied to third-party vendor performance.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

Best,
